exposure: treatment modalities for cesarean scar pregnancy (systemic methotrexate, local methotrexate, potassium chloride injection, laparotomy and wedge resection, uterine artery embolization, intrauterine balloon, expectant management, hysteroscopy and curettage, hysterectomy)
outcome: complications (retained products of conception, failed medical termination, failed curettage)
subsequent pregnancy outcomes (recurrent cesarean scar pregnancy, term pregnancy, spontaneous abortion, viable normally located pregnancy)
cohort: The study included 26 patients with 30 diagnosed cases of cesarean scar pregnancies at Yale-New Haven Hospital between May 2013 and March 2018.
finding: Women with a cesarean scar pregnancy are at risk for its recurrence in the future, although a normal pregnancy after a cesarean scar pregnancy is also possible.
mod_finding: Patients with a prior cesarean delivery who experience a cesarean scar pregnancy are at risk for recurrence of cesarean scar pregnancy in future pregnancies.
